title: How to turn on memory in ChatGPT on Mac: steps, limits, and what to check
metaTitle: How to turn on memory in ChatGPT on Mac: steps
description: How to turn on memory in ChatGPT on Mac: press ⌘, for Settings, open Personalization, and switch memory on. Plan limits, checks and fixes below.
targetKeyword: how to turn on memory in chatgpt on mac
intro: To turn on memory in ChatGPT on Mac, sign in, press ⌘, to open Settings, choose Personalization, and switch memory on. The switch may already be on, so check it before you change anything.
tldr: Sign in to ChatGPT on your Mac first. Memory needs a signed-in account.
Press ⌘, to open Settings, then select Personalization in the sidebar.
Switch memory on, start a new chat, and ask a question that uses an earlier detail.
Plan limits differ. Free gets limited memory, and Pro gets the maximum listed on the pricing page.

blocks.text: What you need before you turn memory on

Memory belongs to your ChatGPT account, so sign in first. The ChatGPT home page says you need to sign in to save chats, and memory needs a signed-in account too. If you use ChatGPT on the web and on your Mac, use the same account in both. Otherwise you will compare two different sets of settings and wonder why they do not match.

Your plan sets how much memory and context ChatGPT uses. The pricing page gives each plan a short label. Free gets limited memory. Go gets longer memory. Plus gets expanded memory and context. Pro gets maximum memory and context.

blocks.text: Guides disagree about which plans get memory. Some say only Plus, Team, and Enterprise users have it. One reviewer found it on every tier. The pricing page lists memory for Free, Go, Plus, and Pro, so use your own Settings screen as the final check. If the switch is missing, look at your plan and account first.
How memory works in the ChatGPT Mac app

Memory lets ChatGPT carry details from one chat into later chats. You do not have to repeat your job, your tools, or your writing style every time. That saves time on repeat questions. It also means ChatGPT can bring up an old detail at the wrong moment, so you need to read what it keeps.

An arXiv paper called The Algorithmic Self-Portrait looked at 2,050 memory entries from ChatGPT users. The authors report that 96% of the memories were created unilaterally by the conversational system. In plain words, the user did not ask for most of them. Keep that number in mind when you review what ChatGPT has saved.

blocks.title: Check it in a new chat
blocks.text: Start a new chat after you change the switch. Then ask ChatGPT what it knows about you, and compare the answer with what you have shared.
Turn on memory step by step

The steps above list the clicks in order. This section explains what each click is for and what to look for on your screen. Keep the Settings window open while you follow along. Labels are the part most likely to differ between builds.
Open Settings with ⌘,

Settings opens with ⌘, from the app menu. You can also choose ChatGPT > Settings from the menu bar. Both routes open the same window. If ⌘, does nothing, click ChatGPT in the menu bar first so the app is active. Then press the shortcut again.
Find Personalization in the sidebar

Select Personalization in the Settings sidebar. On the web, OpenAI's Learn pages say ChatGPT memory is managed under Settings > Personalization. The guides we read describe the Mac app the same way. We could not open OpenAI's Mac help pages, so confirm the layout in your copy of the app.
Turn on the memory switch

Find the memory switch and turn it on. Third-party guides name two switches, Reference saved memories and Reference chat history. Saved memories are the notes ChatGPT keeps. Chat history lets it use earlier chats. If your build shows both, decide which one you want before you switch them on.
Confirm that memory works

Start a new chat. Ask a question that depends on something you told ChatGPT before, such as your job or a project name. Or ask what it knows about you. If the answer uses earlier details, memory is working. If it does not, check the switches again, then sign out and sign back in.

blocks.title: Do not change the Codex toggle
blocks.text: The ChatGPT Settings reference lists a toggle called Enable Codex memories. That setting belongs to the Codex desktop app. It is not the switch for ChatGPT chat memory, so leave it alone for this task.
Check the default before you change anything

Sources disagree on whether memory starts on or off. One guide says it is off. A TechRadar reviewer also found it off. Accounts may differ, so look at the switch before you touch it. If it is already on, you may not need to do anything. If it is off, switch it on and run the test above.
Temporary Chat and memory

Temporary Chat is a separate option. Press ⌘⇧N to start one in the Mac app. OpenAI's commands reference lists it as New temporary chat, and the shortcut applies to ChatGPT, not Codex. Whether a temporary chat ignores memory is less clear. One OpenAI snippet suggests it does. Some guides say a temporary chat can read memories without creating new ones. We could not confirm either claim, so test it in your own account.
For the full steps, read [how to use temporary chat in ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/use-temporary-chat-in-chatgpt).
Mistakes people make with memory

items: Turning on the Codex toggle and thinking memory is on. Those are two different settings.
Trusting a guide's menu names without checking the window in front of you.
Forgetting that saved entries apply across chats, so old details can appear in new ones.
Skipping the test. A switch that looks right does not prove that memory works.
Assuming every saved entry is accurate. The study found most entries came from the system, so check them.
Treating memory as the only privacy control. Temporary Chat and chat history are separate choices.

blocks.text: These mistakes share one cause. People trust the first label they see. Open the switch, read the label, and test with a real question.
When memory seems to do nothing

Start with sign-in. Memory needs a signed-in account, so a logged-out window will not help. Then check your plan on the pricing page. Free gets limited memory, so less carries over from older chats. Last, check that you are not in a Temporary Chat, because that may not behave like a normal chat.

Some third-party blogs say memory fills up at a set limit. Those limits came from sources we could not check, so do not treat any number as official. OpenAI's pricing page only uses words like limited, longer, expanded, and maximum.
Turn memory off again

Use the same path. Open Settings from the menu bar, select Personalization, and switch memory off. The guides describe chat history as a separate switch, so check that one too if you want less saved. For those steps, read [how to turn off chat history in ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/turn-off-chat-history-in-chatgpt).
Next steps after memory is on

Custom instructions also shape how ChatGPT answers you. Set them if you want a standing set of preferences. See [how to set custom instructions in ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/set-custom-instructions-in-chatgpt). If you share a Mac or a work account, read [how to sign out of ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/sign-out-of-chatgpt-in-chatgpt) as well.
What the research behind the 96% figure does and does not show

The study used chat logs donated through European data access requests. That makes it a sample, not a survey of all ChatGPT users. Its user count also differs between the paper and a news report. Read the numbers as a rough picture, not a precise rate.

faq.question: Is memory on by default in ChatGPT on Mac?
faq.answer: Sources disagree. One guide says it is off, and a TechRadar reviewer also found it off. Check the switch in Settings > Personalization before you change anything. The switch shows the state for your own account, which is the answer that matters.

faq.question: Do I need a paid plan to turn on memory?
faq.answer: The pricing page lists memory for Free too, but with limited memory and context. Some guides say only paid tiers have it. Trust the pricing page for plan rules, and trust your own Settings screen for whether the switch appears.

faq.question: Why does ChatGPT remember things I never asked it to?
faq.answer: The arXiv study of 2,050 memory entries found that 96% were created by the system, not requested by the user. That is why it helps to review what ChatGPT keeps. Fix or remove entries you do not want kept, if your build lets you.

faq.question: Does Temporary Chat use memory?
faq.answer: The sources do not settle it. One OpenAI snippet suggests Temporary Chat ignores memories, but we could not open that page. Test it in your own account before you rely on it for private work.

faq.question: Can I control memory for a single chat?
faq.answer: The per-chat control in OpenAI's Learn pages belongs to Codex, the coding app. For ChatGPT chats, use Temporary Chat if you want a chat kept out of your history, and test whether it skips memory.

faq.question: Why can't I find the memory switch?
faq.answer: Sign in first, then open Settings with ⌘, and select Personalization. If the section is still missing, check your plan on the pricing page. Business and Enterprise do not appear on the page we read.

faq.question: Does turning memory off delete what is saved?
faq.answer: The sources we could open do not say. After you switch memory off, open the same section and check whether saved entries are still there.

faq.question: Is there a shortcut for memory settings?
faq.answer: The sources we read do not list one. ⌘, opens Settings, and you can change app shortcuts under Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts.

steps.name: Sign in to ChatGPT
steps.text: Open ChatGPT on your Mac and sign in with the account you use every day. Memory needs a signed-in account. The ChatGPT home page says you need to sign in to save chats, so start here.
steps.tip: Use the same account on the web so you compare the same settings.

steps.name: Open Settings
steps.text: Press ⌘, while ChatGPT is the active app. The Settings window opens. You can also choose ChatGPT > Settings from the menu bar.
steps.tip: If ⌘, does nothing, click ChatGPT in the menu bar first so the app is active.

steps.name: Open Personalization
steps.text: In the Settings sidebar, select Personalization. On the web, ChatGPT memory is managed in this section. Look for the memory controls here.
steps.tip: If the section name differs in your build, pick the closest match and check it against the guide.

steps.name: Turn on the memory switch
steps.text: Find the memory switch and turn it on. Some guides name two switches, Reference saved memories and Reference chat history. Turn on the ones you want ChatGPT to use.

steps.name: Check your plan limits
steps.text: Open the ChatGPT pricing page in your browser and find the memory row. Free gets limited memory and context. Go gets longer memory. Plus gets expanded memory and context. Pro gets maximum memory and context.
steps.tip: Business and Enterprise do not appear on the page we read, so ask your admin if you use a work account.

steps.name: Test it in a new chat
steps.text: Start a new chat. Ask a question that depends on something you told ChatGPT before. If the answer uses that detail, memory is working.
steps.tip: If you cannot think of a detail, ask what ChatGPT knows about you.

troubleshooting.problem: The Settings window does not open with ⌘,
troubleshooting.fix: Click ChatGPT in the menu bar and choose Settings. If another app has focus, click into ChatGPT first. If it still fails, check Keyboard Shortcuts in Settings for a conflict.
Sign in with your account first. Then check the memory row on the pricing page. Business and Enterprise do not appear on that page, so ask your admin if you use a work account.

troubleshooting.problem: The switch is on, but ChatGPT forgets things
troubleshooting.fix: Start a new chat. Temporary Chat may not use memory, so make sure you are in a normal chat. Ask a direct question about a detail you shared earlier.
Some blogs report a memory limit, but those numbers come from unofficial sources. Review what is saved if your build shows it, and remove old entries you no longer want.

troubleshooting.problem: The labels do not match this guide
troubleshooting.fix: Trust the app. The labels here came from search results and third-party guides, and OpenAI's help pages returned errors during research.

troubleshooting.problem: You want memory off, but chats still feel saved
troubleshooting.fix: Memory and chat history are separate switches in the guides. Turn off the memory switch, then read the chat history guide to limit saved chats too.
